title: FISH Protocol: Filter Hybridization
author: Eva Petrova
materials: Sterilize filtration unit and other equipment.

steps.title: Moisten filters
steps.instruction: Immerse CN support filters and PC filters (shiny side up) in sterile water until fully wet.

steps.title: Place filters in unit
steps.instruction: Transfer the moistened CN and PC filters into the filtration unit, shiny side up.

steps.title: Check planarity
steps.instruction: Verify the planarity of the filtration unit and filters using a water level to ensure even distribution of planktonic cells.

steps.title: Vacuum filter sample
steps.instruction: Apply a gentle vacuum (~150 mbar) to filter 100 mL of water sample (≈10⁵ cells mL⁻¹) through the filters.

steps.title: Fix cells on filter
steps.instruction: Remove the vacuum, overlay each filter with 4 mL of 3 % PFA fixative (mix 3 mL 4 % PFA solution with 1 mL 1× PBS), and incubate for 20 min.

steps.title: Remove fixative
steps.instruction: Apply vacuum to remove the fixative solution.

steps.title: Wash filters
steps.instruction: Perform three wash cycles to remove residual fixative.

substeps.instruction: Add 3 mL 1× PBS and remove by vacuum.
Add sterile water and remove by vacuum.
Repeat the PBS and water washes once more.

steps.title: Dry and label filters
steps.instruction: Using sterile tweezers, remove each filter from the unit, place it shiny side up on a dust‑free Whatman paper to dry, label the shiny side with a pencil, and store at –20 °C until hybridization (filters may be stored frozen for several months). Include a negative‑control run with sterile water.

steps.title: Prepare hybridization buffer
steps.instruction: Make 2 mL of hybridization buffer as described in the reagent list.

steps.title: Add probe to buffer
steps.instruction: Add 3 µL of probe working solution to 27 µL of the hybridization buffer; keep the probe mixture protected from light and on ice.

steps.title: Section filter
steps.instruction: Place each dried filter on a microscopic slide (shiny side up) and cut it with a sterile scalpel into four equal sections; label each section with a pencil.

steps.title: Arrange sections on slide
steps.instruction: Place one or more filter sections shiny side up on a microscopic slide; multiple sections may share a slide and be hybridized with the same probe.

steps.title: Prepare equilibrated chamber
steps.instruction: Put a piece of tissue into a 50 mL tube and moisten it with the remaining hybridization buffer to create an equilibrated chamber.

steps.title: Add hybridization solution
steps.instruction: Deposit 30 mL of hybridization solution onto each filter section, lay the slide horizontally inside the 50 mL tube, and close the lid tightly.

steps.title: Hybridization incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the sealed tube at 46 °C for at least 90 min in a hybridization oven.

steps.title: Prepare washing buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare 50 mL of washing buffer in a 50 mL plastic tube and pre‑heat it to 48 °C.

steps.title: Wash hybridized sections
steps.instruction: Quickly transfer the filter sections into the warm washing buffer and incubate for 15 min at 48 °C in a water bath.

steps.title: Rinse and dry sections
steps.instruction: Using sterile tweezers, pick up each section, rinse briefly (several seconds) in sterile double‑distilled water, and dry on Whatman paper.

steps.title: Counterstain sections
steps.instruction: Stain nucleic acids and prepare sections for microscopy.

substeps.instruction: Cover each section with 80 µL of SYBR Green I or DAPI solution and incubate 10 min on ice in the dark.

steps.title: Mount for microscopy
steps.instruction: Place the dried section on a glass slide, add 1–2 drops of antifadent, cover with a microscope cover slip, and allow the antifadent to spread (avoid bubbles and excess antifadent).

steps.title: Image samples
steps.instruction: Observe the slides under an epifluorescence or confocal laser‑scanning microscope using appropriate filters or lasers.

steps.title: Store mounted slides
steps.instruction: Slides in antifadent may be stored at 4 °C (do not freeze) for several days; alternatively, remove antifadent with water, dry the slides, and store at –20 °C for longer periods (probe fluorescence fades faster than DAPI).

steps.title: Quantify cells
steps.instruction: Perform manual counting: (1) count DAPI‑stained cells in ≥50 random microscopic sections for absolute totals; (2) for relative abundances, count DAPI‑ and probe‑stained cells in 20 random sections at 400× (DAPI) and 1000× (probe), viewing weak signals first with FLUOS filter, then Cy3, then DAPI; count ≥500 DAPI cells to keep error <±5 %; subtract counts from negative‑control probe NON338; calculate the ratio of probe‑labeled cells to total DAPI cells per section.
